result.rationale: The code is `if (discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1) { return; }` — the check requires the attacker's *origin* to be a substring of discourseUrl, not the reverse. An origin like 'https://evil-forum.com.attacker.com' would only pass if discourseUrl literally contained that full origin string, which it wouldn't unless the attacker controlled the site's own configured URL. The described bypass ('evil-forum.com.attacker.com passing verification') requires the opposite check (`e.origin.indexOf(discourseUrl)`), which is not what the diff shows. Also, even a successful spoof only controls the ifra

adjudication.rationale: In app/assets/javascripts/embed.js, origin validation is `if (discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1) { return; }`, which accepts any sender whose `e.origin` is a substring/prefix of `discourseUrl`. This is not an exact origin match, so a different origin like `https://forum.co` would pass when `discourseUrl` is `https://forum.com`, allowing a malicious window to spoof `discourse-resize` messages.
